name: MK-434

card.summary: A discontinued experimental 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor from the 1990s that lowers DHT, the hormone linked to androgenetic hair loss, discussed as a potential hair-retention compound.
card.note: Never marketed; studied mainly in animals with one early single-dose human study. Not an approved drug.

quick.overview:
MK-434 (also written MK-0434) is an experimental steroid 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor that was studied in the 1990s. These enzymes convert testosterone to dihydrotestosterone (DHT), the androgen implicated in male pattern hair loss, so the compound is of interest to people who want to keep their hair.
Published work is mostly in rats, dogs and birds, plus one early single-dose study in healthy men that found DHT dropped by roughly half. It is not an approved medicine and is not sold as one.
quick.how: There is no approved use and no clinical protocol. Its appearance in hair-loss discussion comes from its mechanism, which is similar in kind to finasteride and dutasteride.
quick.risks: Safety in humans beyond single doses has not been reported. Because it is unapproved, there is no label, regulator guidance or prescribing information.

lead: MK-434, also written MK-0434, is a steroidal inhibitor of 5-alpha-reductase, the enzyme that converts testosterone to dihydrotestosterone (DHT). Because DHT is the main androgen behind androgenetic alopecia, 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors are used to preserve hair; MK-434 is of interest in hair discussions for the same mechanism.

In a single-rising-dose study of healthy men, MK-0434 reduced DHT by about 50% at doses above 5 mg, with the maximum effect at 24 hours maintained through 48 hours, and it did not change serum testosterone; it was described as well tolerated at single doses up to 100 mg [1].

The compound has otherwise been used in animal research. In hyperplastic dog prostates it shrank glandular tissue slightly more than finasteride [2], and in rats it blocked prostate growth from testosterone without blocking testosterone's muscle, fat and bone effects [3][4]. No hair-loss trials are listed.

chain: Lower DHT, the androgen linked to follicle miniaturisation
angle.text: The hair link is mechanistic: lowering DHT is how finasteride-type drugs work against pattern hair loss. MK-434 has been studied for DHT lowering, not for hair outcomes.

paras: MK-0434 inhibits 5-alpha-reductase. In healthy men it reduced circulating DHT by about half without altering serum testosterone [1]. A zebra finch study reported it also reduced aromatase and 5-beta-reductase activity in vivo [5].

In castrated rats given testosterone, MK-434 prevented prostate DHT build-up and enlargement while grip strength, hemoglobin and other anabolic effects were preserved [3]. A separate rat study found testosterone's effects on body weight, fat and bone resorption markers were not blocked by MK-434 [4]. These studies concern prostate and anabolic effects, not hair.
In adolescent male rats, MK-434 did not impair adult social interaction, unlike an aromatase inhibitor and an antiandrogen [6].

One single-dose study in healthy male volunteers, covering 0.1 to 100 mg, measured pharmacokinetics and DHT lowering and reported no significant adverse effects [1]. No hair-loss trial has been found; other research is in animals [2][3][4][5][6].

timeline.event: Single-dose study in healthy men reports ~50% DHT reduction [1].
Dog prostate study compares MK-0434 with finasteride [2].
